details: Equation (2.5) is a chain containing first an equality of probabilities and then a one-sided upper bound.
The target event is the upper-tail event ∑_{i=1}^N a_i X_i ≥ t; no absolute value, lower tail, or two-sided event appears.
Strict positivity of λ makes x ↦ exp(λx) strictly increasing, so exponentiating preserves the ≥ comparison and yields the stated event equality.
The right-hand threshold in the transformed event is exp(λt), with the same λ and t as in the original event.
Markov’s inequality is applied to the nonnegative random variable exp(λ∑_{i=1}^N a_i X_i) at the positive threshold exp(λt).
Dividing by exp(λt) produces exactly the prefactor exp(−λt) multiplying the expectation.
The X_i are random quantities, while the a_i, t, and λ are deterministic parameters in the displayed bound.
The same weighted sum ∑_{i=1}^N a_i X_i occurs in the original event, the exponentiated event, and the expectation.
The theorem-level condition t ≥ 0 and proof-local normalization ∥a∥₂ = 1 remain inherited context even though the Markov calculation itself is valid more generally.

contract_plain_english: Under the assumptions of Theorem 2.2.2, fix any positive λ. Because exponentiation by λ is increasing, the event that the weighted Bernoulli sum is at least t is exactly the event that its exponential is at least exp(λt). Markov’s inequality then bounds this probability by exp(−λt) times the moment generating function E[exp(λ∑_{i=1}^N a_i X_i)].
